## 2B.6 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Mostly truthful and restrained.** The public record shows Marcos describing South China Sea and security risks in a way that was mostly **fact-based, bounded, and paired with de-escalation**, not fear-mongering or misinformation to build support for conflict. I found **no credible evidence** that he manipulated intelligence, historical grievance, or false threats. The main caution is a deterrence-heavy security posture, but that is not the same as deceptive threat inflation.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [Marcos threat has grown in South China Sea, Philippines must do more to defend territory](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/901032/marcos-threat-has-grown-in-south-china-sea-philippines-must-do-more-to-defend-territory/story/owl.video.play.png) - GMA News Online / Reuters, 2024-03-19 | Marcos used firm language about a growing South China Sea threat, but also said invoking the MDT would not serve a purpose unless the situation became “existential.” This is credible threat explanation with an explicit threshold, not panic or fabricated danger. | `2B.6`, `2B.3`, `1B.8` |
| E2 | Favorable | [PH, Viet Nam sign agreements on rice trade, agriculture, SCS incident prevention and management](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-01-30 | Marcos’s Vietnam visit produced a formal incident-prevention agreement and coast-guard cooperation. That suggests he was publicly treating the threat as a manageable operational problem, not using it to whip up fear. | `2B.6`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E3 | Favorable | [China, Philippines agree on 'provisional arrangement' for South China Sea resupply missions, Manila says](https://www.theprint.in/world/china-philippines-agree-on-provisional-arrangement-for-south-china-sea-resupply-missions-manila-says/2184146/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-07-21 | Manila and Beijing agreed to a provisional arrangement and framed it as de-escalation through dialogue. This is evidence that Marcos publicly described the issue as one for diplomacy, not propaganda. | `2B.6`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E4 | Favorable | [Philippines president orders de-escalation in South China Sea, military chief says](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/philippines-president-ferdinand-marcos-jr-orders-de-escalation-south-china-sea-4456701) - CNA / Reuters, 2024-07-04 | After a flare-up, Marcos ordered the armed forces to defuse tensions. That is consistent with truthful crisis communication and inconsistent with using alarms to justify escalation. | `2B.6`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E5 | Favorable | [We’re ordered not to be provoked by China’s aggressive actions in WPS - PCG](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/were-ordered-not-to-be-provoked-by-chinas-aggressive-actions-in-wps-pcg/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-05-04 | A PCG official said personnel were under a chain of command and ordered not to be provoked. This supports the view that the administration emphasized discipline rather than fear-driven mobilization. | `2B.6`, `2B.4`, `1B.8` |
| E6 | Favorable | [Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-06-23 | Marcos said the Philippines was not in the business of instigating wars and would settle disputes peacefully. That is direct evidence against manipulating public fear to build support for conflict. | `2B.6`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E7 | Limiting context | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and included cyber/information-warfare training. This shows a harder deterrence posture and could be used rhetorically to amplify threat perception, but the reporting does not show false claims or misinformation. | `2B.6`, `1B.3`, `1B.9` |
| E8 | Limiting context | [Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism country report: Philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) - Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, 2024-06-17 | The country report notes red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos. That is relevant background because it can distort the information environment, but it is not direct proof that Marcos used misinformation to build support for conflict. | `2B.6`, `1B.8` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 2B.6:** Marcos consistently framed the South China Sea threat as real but bounded, and repeatedly paired that framing with **de-escalation, diplomacy, and incident-prevention**.
- **Best evidence against 2B.6:** I found **no reliable evidence** that he manipulated intelligence, historical grievance, or misinformation to manufacture support for conflict.
- **Search gap:** I did **not** find a credible report of Marcos distorting threat assessments or using false claims to mobilize conflict support in 2024. The available evidence is mostly the opposite: public restraint language, diplomacy, and incident management.

**Working judgment for 2B.6:** **Yes, mostly.** Marcos appears to have explained security threats **truthfully and cautiously**, with no solid evidence of manipulative threat inflation.
